participants were excluded from the Rutgers sample, leaving a total of 31 Western

participants to give causal-historical responses on both the Tsu Ch’ung Chih probe (Ȥ 2(1,
N=72) = 3.886, p< .05) and on the Gödel probe (Ȥ 2(1, N=72) = 6.023, p< .05).10 ... In the pilot study, we found that

notes: Identity assessment: supplied candidate is a full primary manuscript (14 manuscript pages, methods/results, references and appendix), titled Semantics, Cross-Cultural Style, authored by Edouard Machery, Ron Mallon, Shaun Nichols and Stephen P. Main Gödel summary test is t(70)=-2.55, p<.05, whereas Jonah summary test is t(69)=.486, n.s.; individual Gödel-probe chi-square tests explicitly print N=72. Footnote 10 pilot reports Western N=19, Chinese N=32 and t(43)=-3.366, p<.01. No target selected by numbers or order. Candidate arithmetic only: main stated groups 31 + 41 = 72, but the subsequent additional exclusion makes final-group interpretation uncertain; pilot reported group counts 19 + 32 = 51, but these are not established as mutually exclusive final analytic groups for the printed pilot test. Neither sum is adopted as analytic N, and main/pilot samples are not pooled. A main-model candidate N=72 is retained for parent field-scope review only; target_match remains null and confidence false.
